<STRUCT_0001>
We can partly explain the meaning of conditions (S1) and (S2) in terms of
fibre categories. Suppose that <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> are
ring maps in <MATH_0003> with <MATH_0004> surjective.
Denote <MATH_0005> the projection maps.
Assume a choice of pushforwards for <MATH_0006> has been made.
Then the commutative diagram of rings translates into a <MATH_0007>-commutative diagram
<MATH_0008>
of fibre categories whence a functor
<MATH_0009>
into the <MATH_0010>-fibre product of categories.
Condition (S1) requires that this functor be essentially surjective.
The first part of condition (S2) requires that this functor be a
essentially surjective if <MATH_0011> equals the map <MATH_0012>.
Moreover in this case, the second part of (S2) implies that two objects
which become isomorphic in the target are isomorphic in the source
(but it is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>not<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> equivalent to this statement).
The advantage of stating the conditions as in the definition
is that no choices have to be made.

Let <MATH_0001> be a category cofibered in groupoids over <MATH_0002>. Then <MATH_0003> satisfies (S1) if the condition of (S1)
is assumed to hold only when <MATH_0004> is a small extension.
